On Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 11:03 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karthik/Neha — forwarding redlines from EpiCore. Key asks summarized below and my initial read:

Thanks for the summary. Quick legal notes (high level):

- Subprocessors (3.2): we should not accept language that requires prior written consent for every new subprocessor; that is operationally blocking. Propose a compromise: prior notice plus an objection window (10 business days) limited to material categories (e.g., cross-border transfers, analytics). We can document the objection process in the DPA exhibit.
- Data residency: acceptable for a pilot if we tie it to the Order Form (SOW) and clearly mark it as contractual option with associated costs. We must avoid a representation that all production data will be stored in EU unless we actually provision dedicated nodes.
- 90-day log retention: privacy team should weigh in, but my view is: acceptable for limited diagnostic logs if scope/timebound and logs are encrypted and access-controlled.
- SCCs: fine to include as DPA exhibit; ensure we use the latest EU Commission standard text and track execution (signature page).

I'll draft a proposed redline and timeline: internal sign-off by next Tue (4/27), counter to EpiCore Wed (4/28), legal/ops call Thurs (4/29). Please attach any technical notes about residency impacts (latency/cost).

Attaching my comments: soojin_karthik_comments_20270422.docx.

-Karthik
